A name that is declared and never read is dead code. Often it points at a mistake: a result you forgot to return, an import left behind after an edit, or a typo that made two variables out of one.

"Used" means read, so a variable that is only assigned to is reported. Exported names are not. Unlike ESLint's `no-unused-vars`, this rule also checks types, interfaces, and enums, and it knows that `options: Options` uses `Options`.

To keep a name that you do not use, start it with `_`.

This rule is on by default in TypeScript files.

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 4} */}
```ts
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

interface Options {
  retries: number;
}

let attempts = 0;
attempts = attempts + 1;

function retry() {}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```ts
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

interface Options {
  retries: number;
}

export async function load(path: string, options: Options) {
  let attempts = 0;
  while (attempts < options.retries) {
    attempts = attempts + 1;
  }
  return readFile(path);
}
```

A value that is only used in a type, through `typeof`, is reported. Nothing reads it when the code runs:

{/* bad */}
```ts
const defaults = { port: 3000 };

export type Settings = typeof defaults;
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `vars` | `"all"` | `"local"` skips variables in the global scope. The top level of a module is not the global scope, so this only matters for scripts. |
| `varsIgnorePattern` | `"^_"` | Regular expression for names of variables that may be unused. |
| `args` | `"after-used"` | Report unused parameters after the last one that is used. `"all"` reports every unused parameter, `"none"` reports none. |
| `argsIgnorePattern` | `"^_"` | Like `varsIgnorePattern`, for parameters. |
| `caughtErrors` | `"all"` | `"none"` allows an unused `error` in `catch (error)`. |
| `caughtErrorsIgnorePattern` | `"^_"` | Like `varsIgnorePattern`, for the parameter of `catch`. |
| `destructuredArrayIgnorePattern` | `"^_"` | Like `varsIgnorePattern`, for names in `const [a, b] = list`. |
| `ignoreRestSiblings` | `true` | Allow unused names next to a `...rest` in object destructuring. |
| `ignoreClassWithStaticInitBlock` | `false` | Allow an unused class that has a `static {}` block, which runs anyway. |
| `ignoreUsingDeclarations` | `false` | Allow unused `using` and `await using` variables, which are disposed of anyway. |
| `reportUsedIgnorePattern` | `false` | Report a name that matches one of the patterns and is used. |
| `enableAutofixRemoval` | `{ "imports": false }` | With `imports: true`, `--fix` removes unused imports. |

A string in place of the object, `"all"` or `"local"`, sets `vars`.

The options you set replace all of the defaults, so repeat the patterns you want to keep. With an ESLint config the defaults are ESLint's: no patterns, and `ignoreRestSiblings` is `false`.

By default, a parameter in front of one that is used is allowed, because you cannot remove it without moving the others:

{/* good */}
```ts
export const doubled = [1, 2, 3].map((value, index) => index * 2);
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"args": "all"}]} */}
```ts
export const doubled = [1, 2, 3].map((value, index) => index * 2);
```

A name that starts with `_` is unused on purpose. Options of your own have to say so again:

{/* good */}
```ts
export function onMessage(_event: string) {}
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"args": "all"}]} */}
```ts
export function onMessage(_event: string) {}
```

{/* good {"options": [{"args": "all", "argsIgnorePattern": "^_"}]} */}
```ts
export function onMessage(_event: string) {}
```

`ignoreRestSiblings` is for taking properties out of an object:

{/* good */}
```ts
export function publicFields(user: { name: string; password: string }) {
  const { password, ...rest } = user;
  return rest;
}
```

{/* bad {"options": [{"varsIgnorePattern": "^_", "reportUsedIgnorePattern": true}]} */}
```ts
const _port = 3000;

export const url = `http://localhost:${_port}`;
```

With an oxlint config, the rule follows oxlint where the two differ:

- Without an options object, variables and parameters that start with `_` are ignored.
- A value that is only used through `typeof` in a type counts as used, unless `reportVarsOnlyUsedAsTypes` is `true`.
- `fix` takes the place of `enableAutofixRemoval`. It is `{ "imports": ..., "variables": ... }`, and each is `"off"`, `"suggestion"` (default), `"fix"`, or `"safe-fix"`.
